prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; aircraft loading excluded. States: operational hold/safe stop; no explicit modes. Elements/flows: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages flight-associated bags; Bag Tag Printer produces tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacement requires authorized identity-confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight/destination/date/timing; Flight Cutoff Advisory→Baggage Control System (Velvet), authoritative identity/flight/screening/handling recorder, routing/alarming, checked-reentry authorizer; reports missing/duplicate/delayed events. Transfer Bag Feeder accepts verified-identity/onward-flight transfers. Late Transfer Bag Card→Bag Reconciliation Station: verifies identity/location/flight, compares expected population, flags missing/duplicate/unmatched/count discrepancies; Bag Match Query→Airline Ramp Coordinator for mismatch review. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns screening-preserving routes, reports states/alarms; Recovery Route Card→Maintenance Technician before return-to-service. Induction Tray Conveyor meters readable/valid-route bags. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) records tags/images; South Gate Scanner verifies identity; Manual Rescan Receipt/Oversize Exception Ticket→Image Resolution Desk for authorized recapture/position verification, image assessment/disposition. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) routes cleared/diverts unresolved bags; Chute Occupancy Note→Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern). Secondary Inspection Chute controls examination/retention. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver controlled reconciled flows. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) preserves positions/order; Carousel Release Slip←Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms flight/position/resources/sequence. Outbound Load Control Desk accepts consistent flight/count/status records. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) secures/assesses/directs response; Custody Seal Log→Security Duty Manager: accountability/escalation/hold/access resolution. Tern coordinates actors/security/ground-operations, approves exceptions, assigns hold/route owners, stops unsafe induction. Requirements: authorized access; continuous custody; preserved bag-flight association; uncertainty→hold/inspection/escalation; both scanners healthy or feed held. Release requires valid screening/destination. Loading requires readable identity/current flight/security permission; unexplained physical-record differences block acceptance. Departure requires recorded screening-release/custody/reconciliation/loading-check completion. Monitoring: throughput/availability/queues/screening/exceptions; induction

New part:
S238: The Transfer Bag Feeder is monitored for feed rate, interruptions, and backlog against its scheduled demand.
S239: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is monitored for operating state, accumulation, and the time required to clear assigned work.
S240: The East Make-Up Conveyor and the West Make-Up Conveyor are assessed separately so that a local fault does not obscure the condition of the other conveyor.
S241: Tern reviews the operating dashboard and confirms that material service degradation has been assigned an owner and response priority.
S242: The Maintenance Technician investigates equipment faults that exceed the approved recovery interval and records the corrective action taken.
S243: The Security Duty Manager assesses any condition that could compromise screening coverage, security controls, or custody continuity.
S244: The Explosives Response Team is escalated to when an unresolved security condition requires its response under airport procedures.
S245: Service measures include availability, bags processed per operating interval, queue age, screening completion, and unresolved reconciliation differences.
S246: Thresholds and reporting intervals are established in the approved operating plan and reviewed against demand, flight schedules, and safety constraints.
S247: A degraded mode may be used only when the remaining equipment and procedures preserve required screening, traceability, custody, and reconciliation controls.
S248: Operations must suspend the affected activity when required controls cannot be maintained or when an unverified equipment state could misroute baggage.
S249: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates escalation to maintenance, security, and airline operations according to the severity and operational impact of the condition.
S250: Return to service requires the fault to be corrected, required functional checks to pass, alarms to clear, and affected records to be reconciled.
S251: The responsible operational and technical personnel confirm that screening and custody controls are effective before normal routing resumes.
S252: The recovery is monitored at increased frequency until performance is stable and outstanding exceptions have been resolved or formally assigned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
